text:
ting: heads-up — thinking about live panel preview feature for dashboards (WIP UX). Need to figure RBAC consistency when we materialize previews during canary rollouts.

samir: can you sketch the flow? are previews generated by same query path as production panels?

ting: yeah that's the question. current idea: separate preview worker that runs smaller queries, reuses the query-engine but bypasses some cache layers for speed. problem: RBAC enforcement happens at query-gateway; preview worker sits downstream so we'd need to duplicate checks.

penny: duplication increases surface for bugs. If preview bypasses gateway we either replicate authz or call gateway sync which adds latency.

mike: what about a tokenized preview path: preview requests carry an ephemeral token minted by gateway after authz check. preview worker validates signature only. No full policy evaluation.

jaya: that'd be faster but we must ensure tokens can't be used to escalate. Token scope must include panel_id, user_id, expiry, and claim hash of query params.

ting: sketch of token payload:
```json
{"sub":"user:123","panel":"panel:987","exp":1680000000,"claims":{"filters":"hash(...)"}}
```

samir: OK but where do we check row-level predicates? gateway must compute predicate and embed in token. If predicates change (ABAC policy update) old tokens are invalid — that's fine with short TTL.

penny: TTL needs to be tiny (seconds). For live-edit preview user expects <1s roundtrip though, so short TTL fine.

mike: still worry about canary: when we roll out a query-layer change, preview worker might run new query shape while gateway minted token for old predicate semantics.

jaya: that's an important mismatch. We should version tokens with a policy_schema_version field. Gateway includes the current policy SHA and preview worker rejects if mismatched.

ting: good call. policy mismatch -> trigger gateway fallback: run preview through gateway proxy (synchronous) which enforces policy but slower. That gives safe behavior during rollouts.

samir: so route table: preview_worker validates token && policy_version==current -> fast path. else -> gateway proxy slow path. That minimizes risk.

penny: observability — we need metrics: preview.fast_path_rate, preview.policy_mismatch_rate, preview.gateway_fallback_latency. Also count of token_forgeries.

mike: deploy plan: feature-flag preview fast-path behind canary. Start with policy_version check strict, ramp up.

ting: edge cases: shared panels (team dashboards) with mixed tenant access. Token must include team claim and an allowlist check.

jaya: confirm: tokens signed via KMS key rotated via secrets manager; preview worker only needs public key. Rotation race? stamp new tokens with key_id.

samir: ops runbook: if we detect a spike in policy_mismatch_rate during rollout, auto-disable fast path and redirect to gateway proxy.

penny: are we OK with minor duplication of policy logic? gateway will continue to be source of truth; preview worker only verifies token and policy_version.

ting: next steps: write RFC sketch with dataflow diagram, token format, TTL defaults (2s), policy_version semantics, metrics, and rollout plan. I'll start a draft.

mike: ping me when draft is up — I'll validate threat model.

deploy-bot: New draft RFC created: link https://rfc.internal/preview-fastpath-2026 (automated)

ting: thanks. let's sync Wed 11am for quick walkthrough.
